official.deadline_note: No calendar deadline is published for the next cycle. The programme runs an annual three-stage process with approximate dates: Stage 1 preliminary applications around June/July, Stage 2 detailed applications around mid-September to mid-October, Stage 3 interviews around November/December. Applications for the 2027/28 academic year are now closed. The separate Ireland-Palestine Scholarship Programme remained open until 20 October 2026 at 23:59 Irish time.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle; applications for the 2027/28 academic year are now closed
official.status_note: The official applicants page states "Applications for 2027/28 are now closed for the Africa, Latin America, SIDS, and Asia streams."
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award covers programme fees, flights, accommodation and living costs for a one-year master's level programme at a higher education institution in Ireland.
benefits: A fully supported calendar of orientations, social and networking events, support and a suite of specifically designed trainings in areas such as leadership, conflict management and project management
Leadership and professional development training during the year, plus cultural activities and networking with Fellows from a wide variety of countries and disciplines
A volunteering programme, and the option to become an IFP social media ambassador
eligibility: National of a country eligible for the relevant strand
Early to mid-career professional with leadership potential
All eligibility criteria for the relevant strand must be met for applications to be considered
Some fellowships are by invitation only, with embassies inviting applications from staff in designated partner organisations; unsolicited applications in those countries will not be considered
requirements: Meet all eligibility criteria relevant to your country
Secure a place on an eligible master's level programme at an Irish higher education institution
Apply only through the Embassy or channel named for your strand
Complete all three stages of the annual application process
documents: Stage 2 detailed application form, submitted only on invitation from the Embassy, including originals of all required documents
IELTS certificate or equivalent as required by Irish higher education institutions
selection_criteria: The programme focuses on courses that build capacity to deliver the Sustainable Development Goals in the Fellow's home country
Aims are to nurture future leaders, develop in-country capacity to achieve national SDG goals, and build positive relationships with Ireland
The programme promotes gender equality, equal opportunity and welcomes diversity, aligned with SDG 16 on building effective, accountable and inclusive institutions

Particular encouragement is given to applications from the broadest possible base, including applicants with disabilities and applicants from minority or disadvantaged groups, and to increasing the representation of female applicants and those whose gender identity does not align with the male/female gender binary
coverage: Training, orientation, social and networking events
application_method: Stage 2 - detailed application, only if the Stage 1 application is successful: the Embassy invites the applicant to complete a more detailed application form including the submission of originals of all required documents (approximately mid-September to mid-October annually)
official.application_route: Identify your strand and eligible-country list, then apply through the Embassy of Ireland responsible for your country, starting with the Stage 1 preliminary application.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be nationals of a country eligible for the relevant strand. Eligibility is set per strand by eligible country and subject area, and some strands are by invitation only from designated partner organisations.
official.international_eligibility: Open to nationals of eligible developing countries across the Africa, Asia, Latin America, SIDS and country-specific strands (Kader Asmal for South Africa, Roger Casement for Nigeria, Sean McBride for Namibia, Archbishop Michael Courtney for Burundi, Frank Ferguson Fellowship in Engineering for Zambia, and the Ireland-Palestine Scholarship Programme for Palestine).
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Each strand has its own eligible countries and subject areas; the Frank Ferguson Fellowship in Engineering is restricted to Zambia and to engineering. Applicants may only apply under the strand matching their country, and Belize candidates must use the Central America Award rather than the SIDS Fellowship.
official.duration: One year. Eligible master's level programmes commence in August or September each year and, depending on the programme, run for between 10 and 16 months.
official.description: The Ireland Fellows Programme offers people from around the world the opportunity to spend one year studying in Ireland, and is fully funded by the Irish Government under the auspices of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. It is designed to give early to mid-career professionals with leadership potential a world-class education that contributes to capacity building in their home countries, and is managed by the Embassy of Ireland responsible for each applicant's eligible country.
official.region: Ireland (Europe) as the place of study; eligible strands cover Africa, Asia, Latin America and Small Island Developing States
official.program_type: Fully funded one-year master's level fellowship for early to mid-career professionals
official.english_requirement: Irish higher education institutions require applicants to have an International English Language Testing System (IELTS) certificate or equivalent; early preparation for the IELTS exam is strongly advised, even for native English speakers.

applicant_utility.summary: Everything hinges on your strand and your country: the programme is administered strand by strand through a specific Embassy of Ireland, and some strands are invitation only, so an unsolicited application in those countries will simply not be considered. The award is genuinely comprehensive - programme fees, flights, accommodation and living costs - but it operates in three stages, and you only reach the detailed Stage 2 form if your Stage 1 preliminary application succeeds. With 2027/28 closed, the practical action now is to watch the applicants page through June and July, and to get IELTS booked well before then because the programme explicitly advises early preparation even for native speakers.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early to mid-career professionals from an eligible strand country with a clear leadership record and a Master's choice that builds capacity towards the SDGs in their home country.
application_readiness_checklist: Find your country on the applicants page strand list and confirm which award you fall under before anything else - the Frank Ferguson Fellowship in Engineering, for example, is Zambia only
Check whether your country's strand is invitation only, and if so build the relationship with the designated partner organisation rather than preparing an open application
Book IELTS as early as possible and aim to hold the certificate before Stage 2, since original documents are required at that point
Choose a Master's programme that starts in August or September and runs 10-16 months, and check it is an eligible programme for your strand
Line up academic and professional referees who can supply originals quickly if you are invited to Stage 2
Map your career story to SDG delivery in your home country, since that is the stated focus of the courses the programme targets
common_rejection_risks: Applying through the wrong channel, or submitting an unsolicited application in a country where the strand is invitation only
Missing one of the eligibility criteria for the strand - all criteria must be met for the application to be considered
Selecting a programme that starts outside the August/September window or runs shorter than 10 months
Arriving at Stage 2 without original documents, since the detailed stage requires originals of all required documents
Leaving IELTS until after the Stage 2 invitation, when the original certificate is needed
Applying under a SIDS strand when your country is assigned to a different award - Belize candidates, for instance, must use the Central America Award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not published. The award covers programme fees, flights, accommodation and living costs, but with no figures given, applicants should budget personally for any cost not explicitly named in the offer, including pre-departure expenses and any costs around dependants.
document_audit: Stage 2 requires originals of all required documents, so keep certified originals accessible rather than scans only
The IELTS certificate must be the Academic version accepted by the specific Irish institution you are applying to
Academic and professional references should be from people who can respond within the short window between the Stage 1 result and the Stage 2 deadline
Because the process is run by the Embassy, confirm the exact document list and format with the responsible mission rather than assuming a standard pack
alerts: Applications for 2027/28 are now closed for the Africa, Latin America, SIDS and Asia streams, so the next opportunity is the following cycle
Do not confuse this programme with the Ireland-Palestine Scholarship Programme, which is a separate award with its own deadline and was open until 20 October 2026
Only if your Stage 1 application is successful will you be invited to Stage 2, so a silent period after Stage 1 is not a rejection but also not a guarantee
The programme is managed by the relevant Embassy, so timelines can differ slightly by country - check with your mission rather than relying on another country's dates
The programme is one of Irish Aid's most longstanding, running for over 50 years with almost 4,000 alumni, so the alumni network is a genuine asset worth referencing in your application
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Stage 1 preliminary application to your strand's Embassy, then on success a Stage 2 detailed application with originals of all documents, then a Stage 3 interview, with decisions communicated through the responsible Embassy.
